rules.statement: When a test asserts that one action happened after another (for example a review request after a push), check the order using recorded state such as the commit the request targeted. Counting how many times the action occurred is not enough.
rules.why: A check that only counts occurrences still passes when the actions happen in the wrong order, for example a review requested before the push that moved the branch.
rules.check: Look for test assertions that count matching events or comments to show a sequenced behavior, with nothing that compares timestamps, commit SHAs or recorded state to prove the order.

rules.statement: In prose workflow instructions or command templates, when a set of conditions deliberately excludes a case (for example a clean first pass getting no recommendation), say so explicitly right after the conditions.
rules.why: An unstated exclusion reads like an oversight: reviewers and readers can't tell whether the behavior is intended, and it may contradict summaries elsewhere.
rules.check: Look for conditional clauses in instruction templates that leave out an obvious case (such as a first or empty pass) without a sentence saying the omission is intentional.
